🔀 Multi-Process Access

Open the same BLite database from multiple processes simultaneously — with full ACID safety, cross-process WAL coordination, and zero configuration.

Overview

By default BLite uses FileShare.None so a second process attempting to open the same file receives an IOException immediately. This keeps the single-process path lean and avoids any shared-memory overhead.

Setting AllowMultiProcessAccess = true on PageFileConfig switches the engine into multi-process mode:

  • The data file and WAL are opened with FileShare.ReadWrite.
  • A .wal-shm sidecar file is created next to the WAL. It carries an atomic transaction-id counter, the published WAL end-offset, a writer-owner PID stamp, and a bounded reader-slot table.
  • Cross-process writer serialisation uses a named Mutex on Windows (Local\BLite_walshm_w_<sha>) and fcntl OFD locks on Linux / macOS. Both primitives are auto-released by the kernel if the owner process crashes.
  • Transaction IDs are allocated from the shared SHM counter so they are globally unique across processes.
  • On open, a stale-PID check clears any writer-owner stamp left by a crashed previous owner.

Quick Start — DocumentDbContext

Pass a PageFileConfig with AllowMultiProcessAccess = true to the base constructor:

using BLite.Core;
using BLite.Core.Storage;

public class AppDb : DocumentDbContext
{
    private static readonly PageFileConfig _cfg =
        PageFileConfig.Default with { AllowMultiProcessAccess = true };

    public AppDb() : base("app.blite", _cfg) { }

    public DocumentCollection<int, Order> Orders => Collection<int, Order>();
}

Every process that opens AppDb with this config co-operates safely on the same file.

Quick Start — BLiteEngine

using BLite.Core;
using BLite.Core.Storage;

var config = PageFileConfig.Default with { AllowMultiProcessAccess = true };
using var engine = new BLiteEngine("app.blite", config);

var orders = engine.GetOrCreateCollection("orders");

PageFileConfig.Server() Preset

For server scenarios where the WAL and index files should live in dedicated sub-directories, use the PageFileConfig.Server() factory. It configures separate wal/ and collections/ directories and is the recommended starting point for multi-process deployments:

var config = PageFileConfig.Server("data/app.blite") with
{
    AllowMultiProcessAccess = true
};

using var engine = new BLiteEngine("data/app.blite", config);

The resulting layout on disk:

data/
  app.blite          ← main database file
  app.blite.idx      ← B-Tree index file
  wal/
    app.wal          ← Write-Ahead Log
    app.wal-shm      ← shared memory sidecar (created automatically)
  collections/
    app/             ← per-collection data files

Lock Timeouts

The LockTimeout property controls how long a writer waits to acquire the cross-process lock before throwing TimeoutException. The default is 500 ms for both reads and writes.

var config = PageFileConfig.Default with
{
    AllowMultiProcessAccess = true,
    LockTimeout = new LockTimeout(readMs: 1_000, writeMs: 3_000)
};

Use LockTimeout.Immediate for fail-fast behaviour — the call throws instantly if the lock is not available:

var config = PageFileConfig.Default with
{
    AllowMultiProcessAccess = true,
    LockTimeout = LockTimeout.Immediate
};

Combined with Encryption

Multi-process mode and AES-256-GCM encryption can be used together. Pass baseConfig to the encryption constructor:

var multiProcessBase = PageFileConfig.Default with { AllowMultiProcessAccess = true };
var crypto = new CryptoOptions { Key = key };

using var engine = new BLiteEngine("secure.blite", crypto, baseConfig: multiProcessBase);

Limitations

ScenarioSupportedNotes
Multiple processes on the same machine✅Full ACID, WAL coordination via SHM + OS locks
Multiple threads within one process✅Always supported, independent of this flag
Blazor WASM / browser runtime❌No filesystem locking, no shared memory — use OPFS/IndexedDB backends instead
Network filesystems (NFS, SMB)❌File-locking semantics are unreliable — keep the database on a local drive

Crash Safety

If a writer process crashes mid-transaction the OS automatically releases the Mutex / OFD lock. The next process to open the database detects the stale PID in the .wal-shm sidecar, clears the writer-owner stamp, and proceeds normally — no manual recovery is required.
